newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi says U.S. changes not related to suits.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi says U.S. changes not related to suits.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motor Corp. said Tuesday the changes of top management at its U.S. subsidiaries are not related to alleged sexual harrassment problems at its Normal, Ill., plant.

Tsuneo Ohinouye, chairman of Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America (MMMA), the automaker's manufacturing arm, is retiring at the end of June after six years in his post, said Gael O'Brien, a spokeswoman for the company in Normal.

Tohei Takeuchi, president of Mitsubishi Motor Sales of America (MMSA), is leaving his post also at the end of June as part of a normal four-year rotation, said Kim Custer, a spokesman for the company's Cypress, Calif.-based marketing arm.
"Somehow the Post drew the conclusion Mr. Takeuchi had been fired. He's being rotated back to Japan as we had expected him to," said Custer.

The Washington Post reported Tuesday the Japanese automaker replaced the officials days after the parent company's board of directors met with former U.S. Secretary of Labor Lynn Martin, who is heading an effort to eliminate possible sexual harrassment problems.

Citing a company source, the paper said the changes were made out of concern that key officials were resisting recommendations from Martin's task force. The U.S. Equal Opportunity Employment Commission filed its largest-ever sexual harrassment case against the company last year.
"That is not the case. He is retiring," O'Brien said of Ohinouye.

O'Brien said Ohinouye, who is 65, has been with the parent firm for 42 years. Mitsubishi typically shifts its executives every four years, announcing the changes each year in late April. Ohinouye will continue to serve as an advisor to both MMMA and MMSA.

As part of the management changes, Mitsubishi has named Michio Yamashita chairman and CEO of both MMSA and MMMA. O'Brien said combining the posts is part of an ongoing strategy to better coordinate the two units in North America.
Custer also said Takashi Sonobe, who was executive vice president of MMSA, is now the subsidiary's president.
